endorsements.title: Developing, purchasing, implementing and monitoring AI tools in radiology: practical considerations. A multi-society statement
endorsements.issuer: ACR, CAR, ESR, RANZCR, RSNA; Radiol Artif Intell 2024 (PMID 38251899, doi:10.1148/ryai.230513)
endorsements.quote: Any change control plan must include robust real-time AI model performance and measures that mitigate patient risk.

endorsements.title: CHAI AI governance frameworks (playbooks)
endorsements.quote: A continuously adaptive or self-calibrating AI system for which the vendor cannot provide defined governance procedures specifying: (a) the criteria under which a calibration change constitutes a governance notification event, (b) the disclosure mechanism for such events, and/or (c) whether such changes trigger re-risk-categorization.

endorsements.title: CHAI Responsible AI Guide (Assurance Standards Guide)
endorsements.quote: As many algorithms continuously learn and are updated, it is also important to establish a process of iterative review and data sharing, similar to the process implemented by the FDA for postapproval monitoring and adverse event reporting.

endorsements.title: Challenges in the Postmarket Surveillance of Clinical Prediction Models
endorsements.quote: If such thresholds need to be set, then they should explicitly consider the causal pathway between the model’s recommendation and the resulting intervention, with supporting evidence pointing to the model as the root cause of the apparent performance decay.

endorsements.title: Total product lifecycle regulatory considerations and recommendations for generative AI-enabled medical devices
endorsements.quote: Pre-specify update triggers, locked tests, non-inferiority margins, and rollback criteria.

endorsements.title: AI Therapy Chatbots in Youth With Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder: A Nurse-Led, Risk-Tiered Policy Framework
endorsements.quote: PCCPs should be updated using drift monitoring and postmarket findings.

endorsements.title: Artificial intelligence virtual cells as a new paradigm in nephrology: from multiomics integration to clinical translation
endorsements.quote: Model stewardship should move beyond static performance reports to monitored deploy ment with prespecified drift thresholds and action plans, including human-in-the-loop overrides.

commentary.bottom_line: Five sources endorse predefined performance-change thresholds for continuously adaptive AI, but no supplied study tests whether such thresholds catch silent performance change or reduce harm. The recommendation rests on expert consensus and regulatory analogy rather than on evaluated outcomes.

perspectives.view: No supplied study tests the practice, and no supplied study documents the hazard. The five endorsements consist of one multi-society guidance statement, two frameworks, and two commentaries. Under GRADE conventions, expert statements do not count as evidence of effect, so the certainty that thresholds improve detection or patient outcomes cannot be rated.

Three sources draw on FDA concepts, including predetermined change control plans, postmarket adverse event reporting, and prespecified update triggers with rollback criteria. The CHAI playbook asks vendors to state whether calibration changes trigger risk recategorization. These sources describe how the practice fits existing oversight models, but none reports whether the approach has worked when applied.

The endorsing sources describe threshold-triggered notification as a way to surface performance change before it reaches patients. No supplied study measures how often self-calibrating models drift, how often thresholds would fire, or whether notification leads to timely correction, so the size of the safety benefit remains unknown.

commentary.research_gap: No study has compared deployments of continuously adaptive AI with and without predefined calibration or performance-change thresholds. Useful studies would measure how often thresholds detect drift, the delay between a performance change and governance notification, false alarm rates, staff time spent on review, and downstream effects on patient harm.
commentary.underserved_note: No supplied study tested the practice in any population, including Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy groups. Because drift may differ across patient subgroups, health systems cannot know from current evidence whether aggregate thresholds would detect performance loss that falls mainly on these populations.
